articles.title: Major Drone Attack Paralyzes Moscow Airports, Flights Delayed
articles.body:
A major wave of Ukrainian strike drones targeted the Moscow region early Saturday morning, Oct. 10, prompting severe aviation restrictions that delayed or canceled hundreds of commercial flights across the Russian capital’s major international airports.
Moscow Mayor Sergey Sobyanin claimed that Russian air defenses intercepted 403 unmanned aerial vehicles directed toward the capital region between 8:30 p.m. local time on Friday and 8:30 a.m. on Saturday.
JOIN US ON TELEGRAM
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official.
Sobyanin stated that the vast majority of incoming drones were neutralized on distant approaches to the capital, while 25 were shot down within the immediate airspace approaching Moscow.
Russian monitoring networks and Ukrainian observers described the overnight assault as one of the largest coordinated drone operations directed against the Russian capital since the start of the full-scale war.
The drone barrage triggered temporary ground stops and flight restrictions across Moscow’s primary civil aviation hubs, with the most severe disruptions recorded at Vnukovo and Sheremetyevo, alongside secondary delays at Domodedovo.
Russia’s federal air transport agency, Rosaviatsiya, confirmed that flight suspensions were lifted at 8:50 a.m. local time, though airlines continued adjusting schedules throughout Saturday morning to clear mounting flight backlogs.
Estimates regarding the scale of the disruption varied across civil aviation tracking monitors.
Yabloko Leader Fined Over Anti-War Slogans on Duma Ballots
Ukrainian monitoring channel Exilenova+ reported that approximately 300 scheduled commercial flights experienced cancellations or prolonged delays, while Russian regional news outlet MSK1 reported that at least 370 flights were delayed across the metropolitan airport cluster.
Systematic pressure on Moscow’s air corridors
The disruption across Moscow’s civil aviation network reflects an expanding Ukrainian operational campaign designed to degrade Russian rear logistics, overwhelm metropolitan air defense coverage, and impose tangible economic costs on the Russian heartland.
By forcing civil aviation authorities to repeatedly activate emergency air closure protocols – designated in Russian aviation procedures as the “Kover” (Carpet) plan – recurrent drone incursions disrupt commercial passenger operations, divert long-haul freight traffic, and strain radar tracking architectures deployed around the Russian capital.
The overnight strikes on the capital region coincide with wider Ukrainian precision strikes targeting Russian strategic logistical nodes and fuel infrastructure.
Overnight into Saturday, Ukrainian strike drones struck the Yug Rusi oil transshipment terminal in Rostov-on-Don, igniting a major fire at an export and military supply hub handling 2.5 million metric tons of petroleum products annually.
Consecutive strikes on Russian tech and data infrastructure
The overnight assault on Moscow follows consecutive Ukrainian drone strikes targeting foundational Russian digital and communications infrastructure in adjacent regions.
On Friday, Oct. 9, Ukrainian strike drones damaged a major data center belonging to Russian technology corporation Yandex in the regional capital of Kaluga, located southwest of Moscow.
Yandex confirmed that several hardware modules were completely disabled, warning users that disruptions to its search, ride-hailing, cloud storage, and corporate digital ecosystems could occur while technical teams assess physical damage.
Kaluga Regional Governor Vladislav Shapsha reported that the Oct. 9 drone waves injured nine people across the province, with five hospitalized following impacts in residential and industrial zones.
The Kaluga strike marked the second consecutive day of precision attacks targeting Yandex’s server infrastructure. On Thursday, Oct. 8, Ukrainian drones hit another Yandex data center situated in Sasovo within the Ryazan region, forcing a complete operational shutdown of the installation.
The resulting server outage produced cascading disruptions across major corporate networks and public services dependent on Yandex cloud hosting, including booking systems operated by Russian Railways (RZhD), mobile network operator MegaFon, and several national media organizations.
The compounding infrastructure damage prompted Yandex shares to drop roughly 4 percent on the Moscow Exchange.

articles.title: Hundreds protests at FedEx Oakland over Israel arms shipments
articles.body:
Breadcrumb
Hundreds protests at FedEx in California over arms shipments to Israel
Three years after the outbreak of Israel’s war on Gaza, hundreds of demonstrators gathered in front of a FedEx building in Oakland, California to protest the shipping company’s arms deliveries to Israel.
FedEx, one of the world’s largest package shipping companies, currently sends weapons parts to Israel for its F-35 fighter jets, which has led to demonstrations against their role in Israel’s assault on Gaza. The shipments have been tracked from Oakland International Airport to their final destination of Nevatim Air Base in Israel.
On a warm Friday morning, demonstrators – represented by members of the Palestinian diaspora, labour unions, students, faith leaders and environmentalists – gathered in front of the FedEx entrance, holding signs reading: “No jets for genocide”, “Stop arming Israel” and “Arms embargo now”.
Speakers of different backgrounds took turns talking about their opposition to FedEx’s shipments of weapons parts to Israel, as well as other grievances with the corporation. Mohamed Shehk, an organiser with Arab Resource and Organising Centre (AROC) Action, spoke before a large crowd of demonstrators,
“We know that this did not start three years ago,” he said. “This genocidal apartheid state of Israel has been attempting to erase us, has been engaged in an ethnic cleansing campaign for 70 years.”
He said, “We’re here demanding that FedEx, this war profiteer, put an immediate end to military cargo being shipped to the apartheid state of Israel.”
He also criticised FedEx’s role in union crackdowns and alleged voter disenfranchisement in their home state of Tennessee.
“It’s also worth noting that FedEx isn’t just engaged in complicity in genocide. They are notoriously anti-union and anti-worker,” he said.
“Everyone remembers earlier this year when the Supreme Court shamefully gutted the Voting Rights Act of 1964. The state of Tennessee was the first state to exploit this ruling. Far-right politicians took the only majority Black district and split it up to weaken the Black vote and silence the Black voice,” he said.
“This why it is important for us to unite across all of these issues in this powerful coalition,” he said. “Solidarity with Palestine means solidarity with workers, solidarity with Black communities, and all communities that are oppressed by the capitalist and colonial class.”
Mick Glenn, a local resident, told The New Arab: “I wanted to make whatever difference I could by being there.”
He added, “The speeches were heartbreaking and motivating. I keep going to these demonstrations, but I hope they don’t have to go on much longer.”
A report by the Palestinian Youth Movement published in August 2025 noted that the Oakland airport is second only to Dallas-Fort Worth for the shipment of weapons parts to Israel.
The 15-page report, based on human rights investigations and on data exports, has found that since January, at least 280 military cargo shipments via FedEx have departed from Oakland International Airport, with Nevatim Airbase in Israel as the final destination. These shipments, supplied by Lockheed Martin, have included F-35 fighter jet components for carrying and releasing munitions and guided weapons.
More specifically, the report found that the shipments were consistently frequent (with only one week of a lull in transfers in six months); the materials delivered are wide-ranging, from lethal systems to small bolts; Nevatim is identified as the final destination for the materials; the shipments are coming from the Defence Logistics Agency in San Joaquín; and F-35s are confirmed to be used by Israel in Gaza.

articles.title: Ukraine, long keeping its weapons at home, now lets 18 arms makers export, approving over 90% of more than 400 applications
articles.body:
Ukraine, which long kept its weapons at home, is now clearing its arms makers to sell abroad. Its Commission on Export Control has granted 18 Ukrainian companies permission to send their finished weapons abroad and has processed more than 400 export applications, with over 90% approved, the National Security and Defense Council says, citing commission head Davyd Aloian.
Ukraine now produces far more weapons than it can afford, with defense production growing from about $1 billion a year at the start of the invasion to a projected $55 billion in 2026.
The exports are reportedly conducted under the Drone Deals framework that President Volodymyr Zelenskyy unveiled in April, which allows controlled sales of surplus weapons to partner countries while the Defense Ministry and General Staff retain first claim to everything the front needs. Some categories already run up to 50% beyond what Ukraine can use or finance.
From a stalled commission to 18 approvals
The commission’s work had been halting. It resumed in February after an eight-month freeze and issued the first permits then, and its updated membership has been working since, Aloian notes.
Building partnerships abroad
Aloian framed the goal as scaling Ukrainian technology rather than one-off deals. The state wants domestic producers to expand abroad while partners get working solutions, he says, and is open to dialogue with the defense industry to fix problems as they arise.
Earlier, an industry group that represents more than 400 companies warned in September that the mechanism was choking. A new 20-to-30% fee on export permits priced Ukrainian goods out of the market, it said, and a joint-production program had stalled with hundreds of foreign bids pending.
Euromaidan Press cannot verify whether the Commission on Export Control has taken the issue into consideration.
The council recently met a UK Defense Ministry delegation to discuss closer cooperation, including a Drone Deal, an anti-ballistic coalition, and joint production, Aloian adds. Reaching foreign markets enables producers to attract new orders and investment, scale up, and build long-term partnerships.

articles.title: Russian strikes in Eastern Ukraine kills 12, authorities say
articles.body:
Rescuers conduct search and rescue operations following a Russian attack that struck a five-storey residential building in Zaporizhzhia. | Daria Nazarova/AFP via Getty Images
A Russian attack that killed at least 17 people including three children in Ukraine are Moscow’s “thanks for the lifting on sanctions on diesel exports,” Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Saturday.
A series of strikes on the south-eastern city of Zaporizhzhia also injured at least 18 people, including three children, Ukraine’s state emergency services said on Saturday afternoon.
“People continue to be searched for under the rubble of destroyed houses. Rescue operations continue,” said Mykhailo Semikin, acting head of Zaporizhzhia regional military administration in a Telegram post.

“Today, Russia expressed its thanks for the lifting of sanctions on diesel exports by dropping five glide bombs on residential buildings in Zaporizhzhia,” Zelenskyy said on X.
The strikes took place just one day after U.S. President Donald Trump announced he would temporarily lift sanctions on Russian diesel in a bid to bring soaring prices down.
Ukrainian officials were meeting on the same day with European and U.S. officials in Miami in a fresh diplomatic push to end the conflict between Russia and Ukraine.
Zelenskyy criticized the deal on Friday and accused Trump of using the peace talks as a “smokescreen” while pursuing a deal with the Kremlin.
Even though the talks were supposed to last two days, the Ukrainian team decided to return home earlier then planned “because they managed to talk everything through earlier,” a senior official familiar with the matter told POLITICO. Ukraine will continue to bomb Russian oil refineries despite US-Russia deals, the official added.
The Ukrainian armed forces said Saturday they struck a major oil facility in Russia’s Samara region overnight.

Zelenskyy is currently busy coordinating with Europeans and preparing several high-level meetings, the official said. He spoke on Saturday with leaders of France, Norway and Finland.
“Russian strikes killed over 80 Ukrainian civilians in two days. Moreover, it has stepped up its hybrid attacks against Europe, both EU Member States and NATO Allies,” Kaja Kallas, the EU’s foreign policy chief, said Saturday. “Suspending sanctions on Russian diesel provides Moscow with more revenues to wage war.”
“On Monday, EU Foreign Ministers intend to approve the biggest set of sanctions listings targeting Russia’s war machine since the start of the war,” Kallas added.

articles.title: US-Ukraine talks in Miami derailed by Putin-Trump diesel deal — media
articles.body:
LONDON, October 10. /TASS/. Two-day talks between US and Ukrainian officials in Miami, Florida were derailed by an energy deal reached by the presidents of Russia and the United States, The Financial Times reported, citing sources.
According to the report, US President Donald Trump’s announcement of the deal took Ukrainian negotiators by surprise. A senior Ukrainian official told the newspaper that the delegation was cutting its trip short instead of holding a second round of talks on October 10.
The US, Ukraine, the E3 countries (the United Kingdom, France and Germany), the European Commission and NATO held talks in Miami on October 9. Kiev was represented by Vladimir Zelensky’s chief of staff Kirill Budanov (designated in Russia as a terrorist and extremist), his deputy Sergey Kislitsa, leader of the Servant of the People party’s parliamentary faction David Arakhamia and Foreign Intelligence Servcie chief Rustem Umerov. The Axios news website reported that US negotiators Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner told Ukrainian officials Washington could restrict Kiev’s access to US intelligence if Ukraine refused to make concessions.

articles.title: US, Ukrainian, European officials discuss ending Russia's war at Miami meeting
articles.body:
U.S., Ukrainian and European officials met in Miami on Oct. 9 to discuss efforts to end Russia's war against Ukraine ahead of winter, on the same day Washington moved to ease restrictions on Russian diesel exports.
Discussions were described by U.S. Special Envoy Steve Witkoff as “constructive”, and covered preparations for winter, including protecting Ukraine's energy infrastructure and maintaining grain exports, as well as security guarantees and longer-term arrangements aimed at preventing future conflict. The topics of Ukraine's postwar reconstruction, economic recovery and potential accession to the European Union were also reportedly covered.
In addition to the United States, representatives from the E3 group of France, Germany and the United Kingdom, the European Commission, Ukraine and NATO took part.
Ukraine's delegation included Presidential Office head Kyrylo Budanov, Foreign Intelligence Service chief Rustem Umerov, presidential adviser Sergiy Kyslytsia and lawmaker Davyd Arakhamia, a negotiating team that has traveled to the U.S. and engaged in such discussions in the past.
Zelensky said on Oct. 8 that the negotiations were expected to last two days, Oct. 9–10, and that he anticipated a briefing from the delegation upon its return to Kyiv on Monday, Oct. 12.
In a post on X, Witkoff said that the talks helped identify areas for further consideration ahead of Washington's next engagement with Russia, but announced no concrete agreements. His statement did not indicate whether further meetings would take place on Oct. 10.
Ukrainian representatives had not publicly released their own account of the meeting at the time of publication.
The meeting coincided with U.S. President Donald Trump's announcement that Russia would supply millions of tons of diesel to the United States and global markets following a call with Russian President Vladimir Putin.
The U.S. Treasury Department subsequently issued a temporary authorization permitting purchases of Russian diesel, drawing criticism from Kyiv and European officials over the potential financial benefit to Moscow.
The Kyiv Independent reported earlier on Oct. 9 that Russia was seeking sanctions relief as part of negotiations over a possible halt to attacks on Ukrainian energy infrastructure. Moscow also wants to link a potential energy truce to ceasefire arrangements in the Black Sea.
The discussions come as Russia intensifies attacks on Ukraine's energy facilities ahead of winter, threatening electricity and heating supplies across the country.

articles.title: USA Threatens to Stop Sharing Intelligence With Ukraine Over Attacks on Russian Oil Refineries — Axios
articles.body:
The U.S. has threatened to stop sharing intelligence with Ukraine if it continues to attack Russian oil refineries.
This was reported by Axios, citing Ukrainian and U.S. officials.
According to a Ukrainian official, during eight hours of talks in Miami on Friday, October 9, U.S. President Donald Trump’s envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner threatened to cut Ukraine off from U.S. intelligence data because it had ignored requests to stop strikes on Russian oil refineries.
A U.S. official denied that such threats were made. According to him, Witkoff and Kushner emphasized that the U.S. is a partner of Ukraine that supplies it with ammunition and intelligence, so Kyiv should not take actions that harm American consumers.
“Attacks on oil refineries hurt Russia, but they also hurt the U.S.,” the U.S. official said.
According to the publication, Trump decided to negotiate with Russia regarding diesel fuel supplies after Ukraine repeatedly rejected U.S. requests to halt strikes on Russian oil refineries. The U.S. side links these attacks to rising fuel prices in the United States.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky had previously told Trump and his envoys that he was ready to halt attacks on Russian oil refineries if Russia stopped striking Ukraine’s power grid.
According to an American official, Trump did not consider the attacks on oil refineries to be equivalent to Russia’s strikes on Ukraine’s power grid.
It should be recalled that in March 2025, the U.S. suspended the flow of intelligence data to Ukraine regarding targets on Russian territory. Following this, in particular, France announced that it was prepared to share its intelligence data with Ukraine in place of the United States.
However, a few days later, during talks in Saudi Arabia, the U.S. and Ukraine agreed to resume the exchange of data.
On October 9, the U.S. Department of the Treasury, acting on Trump’s order, temporarily authorized the supply of Russian diesel fuel to the global market. This followed a statement by the U.S. president regarding an agreement to export 4.8 million metric tons of fuel ‘on a short-term basis.’ The authorization is valid until 12:01 a.m. Eastern Daylight Time on April 7, 2027.
Later, in an interview with Axios, Zelensky said he was stunned by the agreement to supply diesel fuel from Russia, which he called ‘unfair and dishonest’ and an undeserved gift to Russian dictator Vladimir Putin.

articles.title: Zelensky has gone too far – Musk
articles.body:
Zelensky has gone too far – Musk
Tech billionaire Elon Musk has lashed out at Vladimir Zelensky, siding with President Donald Trump, who has warned that Kiev’s continued attacks on Russian oil refineries are worsening a global fuel crisis and hurting American farmers.
Trump has also called for a change of leadership in Kiev, accusing Zelensky of repeatedly rejecting opportunities to end the conflict and deliberately ignoring Washington’s requests.
“We told him, do whatever you want, but don’t hit the diesel fuel, because there’s a big problem, a big shortage. And what does he do? He goes and hits the diesel fuel,” Trump told reporters outside the White House on Saturday. “He wants to make problems for the world… for our farmers, our ranchers, with diesel fuel.”
“Zelensky has gone too far,” Musk wrote on X on Sunday, directly responding to a White House video of the remarks, which were part of Trump’s broader criticism of Zelensky, including his suggestion that “it’s time for Ukraine to get a new president.”
@RapidResponse47 @POTUS Zelensky has gone too far
— Elon Musk (@elonmusk) October 10, 2026
The latest spat erupted after Washington agreed to temporarily lift sanctions on Russian diesel exports following a phone call between Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin on Friday, a move intended to ease a global fuel shortage that has pushed up prices in the US and elsewhere.
Trump reached a diesel deal with Putin after Zelensky ignored at least half a dozen requests from Washington to stop striking Russian refineries, according to Axios. Zelensky denounced Trump’s move as a “weak decision,” while Ukrainian negotiators left the talks in Miami a day early.
Musk’s criticism carries particular weight given Ukraine’s heavy dependence on Starlink, the satellite internet network operated by his company SpaceX. Since 2022, tens of thousands of Starlink terminals have become central to Kiev’s battlefield communications, drone operations and coordination between military units. A complete loss of Starlink access could severely disrupt those capabilities and potentially trigger a major battlefield crisis.
Musk has repeatedly called for a negotiated settlement between Moscow and Kiev, and resisted Kiev’s attempts to expand its use of Starlink for attacks on Russian territory. In 2022, Musk refused to activate the network near Crimea to support a Ukrainian strike on Russia’s Black Sea Fleet, warning that doing so would make SpaceX complicit in a major escalation.
More recently, Zelensky personally appealed to Trump to persuade Musk to authorize Starlink-guided drone strikes deep inside Russia. He also sought a face-to-face meeting with the billionaire during a visit to Washington in July, but Musk refused, The Atlantic reported, citing a source familiar with the discussions.
“Elon keeps saying it’s time to make a deal,” an associate of former Ukrainian Defense Minister Mikhail Fedorov told the magazine.
In an apparent effort to court the billionaire’s favor, Zelensky awarded Musk the Order of Freedom, one of Ukraine’s highest state honors, in August, praising his contributions to protecting lives and strengthening Ukrainian-American relations.

articles.title: Trump calls on Ukraine to replace Zelensky
articles.body:
Trump calls on Ukraine to replace Zelensky
U.S. President Donald Trump told reporters on October 10 that Ukraine needs to find a new president who can “make a deal.”
“You know what I suggest? I suggest they get a new leader who could make a deal because he could’ve made many deals and for some reason he never does… I think it’s time for Ukraine to get a new President.” Trump said.
Trump said the U.S. told Zelensky, “You can do whatever you want to Russia,” but also told him not to strike oil refineries because that was “a world problem.”
“And what does he do? He goes and hits the diesel fuel. He better damn well stop,” Trump said.
Trump criticized Zelensky a day after reaching an agreement with Vladimir Putin on supplying Russian diesel fuel to U.S. and global markets. The U.S. and Russian presidents spoke by phone the day before. The U.S. Treasury Department soon issued a temporary license allowing Russian diesel fuel to reach the global market in circumvention of U.S. sanctions, until April 7, 2027.
Ukraine criticized the diesel deal between Moscow and Washington. Zelensky said that Russia’s decision to allow oil product sales “is an investment in the war.”

articles.title: UK vows to maintain pressure on Russia over Trump-Putin diesel deal
articles.body:
İlayda Çakırtekin
10 October 2026•Update: 10 October 2026
The UK government on Saturday vowed to maintain pressure on Russia following a recently announced diesel deal between US President Donald Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin.
"The UK’s position could not be clearer. We will continue working closely with international partners to ensure Ukraine has the military and financial support it needs to defend itself. We will also maintain pressure on Russia," a UK government spokesperson said in a written statement.
The spokesperson noted that London would maintain pressure through the "toughest sanctions regime" it has ever imposed by increasing the cost of "Putin’s aggression" and supporting efforts to secure peace.
"Ukraine has repeatedly demonstrated it is serious about peace, but Russia has repeatedly rejected full and partial ceasefires while continuing attacks on Ukrainian civilians and energy," the statement added.
Spokesperson further stressed the UK's commitment to supporting Ukraine "for as long as it takes and to working with partners to bring about a durable peace."
Putin and Trump spoke over the phone on Friday. Trump described the conversation as a “highly successful discussion.”
In a post on his Truth Social platform, Trump said the talks resulted in an agreement for Russia to “immediately supply” more than 300,000 tons of diesel fuel to US and global markets.
He said another 500,000 tons would be supplied in November, followed by 1 million tons and an additional 3 million tons “within a short period,” depending on the condition of Russian diesel refineries.
Putin said Russian diesel supplies to US and global markets would benefit the world economy, adding that the two leaders discussed the global energy sector, prospects for resolving the Ukraine war, the situation in Iran, and bilateral relations.
